in_arabic.name: أوثال
in_arabic.long_meaning: أوثال هو اسم عربي يعني الخير والمحبة والتقرب إلى الله، مستمد من الجذر الأثل الذي يفهم على أنه الصلاح والبركة، له أهمية كبيرة في التراث الإسلامي وتقاليد الأسرة المسلمة، حيث يرمز إلى القرب من الله والرضا عنه

in_urdu.name: اوثال
in_urdu.meaning: خیر اور محبت اور اللہ کے قریب ہونا
in_urdu.long_meaning: اوثال ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب خیر اور محبت اور اللہ کے قریب ہونا ہے، جو عربي جڑ اوثل سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب صلاح اور برکت ہے، اس نام کی اہمیت اسلامی روایت اور جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم ثقافت میں بہت زیادہ ہے

in_hindi.name: अवथल

in_hindi.long_meaning: अवथल एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ भलाई और प्रेम और भगवान के पास होना है, जो अरबी मूल अथल से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ शुभ और आशीर्वाद है, इस नाम का महत्व भारतीय मुसलमान समुदाय में बहुत अधिक है और इसका उपयोग परंपरागत रूप से किया जाता है

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Awthal" is a beautiful moniker that carries a rich cultural significance. In many Islamic traditions, birds are seen as mystical creatures with deep symbolic meaning. For instance, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is reported to have said, "The angels will not enter a house in which there is a picture of a living creature" - suggesting that images of birds and other animals are permitted in homes, reflecting their positive place in Islamic culture. Additionally, birds are often featured in Islamic art, poetry, and literature, reflecting their importance in Islamic spirituality and everyday life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the Islamic name "Awthal" is evocative of the free and graceful nature of birds in flight. This name can be seen as a reminder of the spiritual journey of the human soul as it strives towards the divine. In Islamic philosophy, the soul is often compared to a bird that must fly towards the light of God, taking flight from the worldly distractions and limitations that weigh it down. The grace and beauty of birds is a reminder of the potential for spiritual transcendence within each of us, inviting us to soar above the mundane and seek the wisdom and knowledge that comes from a deeper connection with the divine.
